subject.title: Preserve structured ACP backend error kinds instead of mapping all errors to `end_turn`

question: Should non-refusal Gateway chat failures in the ACP bridge reject `session/prompt` with `RequestError`, or should they keep resolving `PromptResponse` while exposing structured failure data through another approved surface?
rationale: The pinned ACP SDK stop-reason union cannot represent timeout or rate-limit directly, and switching resolved prompt responses into JSON-RPC rejections is a client-visible compatibility choice that code review cannot safely choose alone.

options.title: Approve RequestError settlement after fixes
options.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures, but require non-conflicting codes/data, intentional reconnect behavior, focused contract tests, and real ACP proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve resolved prompt responses
options.body: Keep existing resolved `PromptResponse` behavior by default and expose structured failure information only through an explicitly approved metadata or diagnostic surface.

options.title: Pause for a replacement
options.body: Leave the issue open for a maintainer-led or refreshed implementation if the current branch cannot settle the compatibility contract and proof gap.

recommendation.title: Approve RequestError settlement after fixes
recommendation.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures, but require non-conflicting codes/data, intentional reconnect behavior, focused contract tests, and real ACP proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner signal is tied to the recent structured error-kind classification and focused ACP tests, making it the best available routing target for the contract decision.
